summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Tips Sharing: Clothing Details Edition Update P18 ## Introduction In this video, we explore handling clothing and model overlap issues in Marvelous Designer, specifically focusing on creating and adjusting a scarf for a virtual model. ## Opening HANA and Creating Outfits - Double-click on **HANA** to open it. - Navigate to the **GAMUT** folder to add a new casual outfit. - Double-click to add a new scarf. ## Adjusting Particle Diameter - Increase the particle diameter of all selected panels to **15**. - Note that increasing the particle diameter will decrease the number of panels, making them appear stiffer. ## Freezing Panels - Select all panels and choose **freeze** so that all costumes will no longer participate in the simulation. - Be aware that this may still clash with the newly created scarf panels. ## Preventing Overlap - Move all panels in the **2D window** to prevent overlapping. - Use the model screenshot for reference while arranging the panels. ## Drawing the Scarf - Draw a rectangle that covers almost the model's face; the length of the rectangle should match the length of the model’s hands. - The width and length can be adjusted according to your preference. - Position the scarf at the back of the virtual model, as the center of the scarf is typically located there. ## Adjusting the Scarf Structure - Adjust the structure of the arrangement to ensure the scarf is the innermost part. - Eliminate any gaps between the model and the scarf for increased stability. - Ignore the gap between the image and the costume temporarily, as it will make the scarf appear narrower later. ## Editing Texture Direction - Use the **edit texture tool** to click on a panel and observe the direction of the panel's brush stroke. - The arrow direction indicates the shape of the cloth; all shape numbers in the software follow this direction. - Modify the shape reduction to enhance panel stability. ## Simulation Settings - During simulation, the image is temporarily shrunk to **30%** of its original size. - Start the simulation to observe that the scarf appears narrower due to this function. ## Pulling the Scarf - When pulling the scarf, pull one end first. - If clear deformation occurs, add a fixing pin to secure it. - Press the **W key** and click the board to increase the fixing pin. ## Checking for Overlaps - After securing one end, pull the other end while checking for penetration. - Pay attention to any hair that may get caught in the model; small gaps can cause issues. ## Adjusting the Shrink Rate - Once the scarf is stabilized, gradually increase the shrink rate to **60%**. - Avoid making large increases to prevent instability. ## Manually Adjusting Wrinkle Shapes - After finishing adjustments, select the scarf fabric. - In the attribute editor, increase the **friction rate** to prevent the scarf from sliding. ## Tying the Scarf - To tie the scarf, add fixing pins at both ends first. - Drag the fixing pin to cross the scarf and add another pin at the intersection to fix the knot. - Ensure there is extra space below the scarf for wearing it. ## Monitoring Pressure - Open the pressure chart on the left side. - When the pressure turns red, it indicates significant changes; avoid stretching further. - Pull a fixing pin and wait for the scarf to tighten. ## Final Adjustments - After tightening, you can delete the fixing pin used to secure the intersection. - Continue pulling the fixing pin to gradually tighten the scarf. - If the friction rate is low, adjustments may cause rapid tightening, leading to instability. ## Length Adjustment - To adjust the length of the scarf, select both ends of the line and move them. - Utilize the **anti-slip extender** to make minor adjustments without excessive changes. ## Enhancing Wrinkle Effects - For more detailed wrinkle effects, reduce the diameter to **10**. - Use a sewing needle to adjust the distance between two fabric points to tighten the scarf. ## Sewing Technique - After adding the sewing needle, the two ends will be sewn together. - Adjust the length of the line to ensure it remains either unfolded or folded. - Adding more sewing needles can yield better results. ## Final Checks - Ensure to read through the process to check for cracks or holes. - After adjustments, increase the shrink rate to **80%**. ## Fixing Needle Tool - Select the fixed needle tool and double-click along the outer line of the plate in the **2D window** to increase fixed needles along this line. - This helps fix the position of the needle. ## Wrinkle Accumulation - Change the shrink rate to **110** to accumulate wrinkles in the area. - You can delete the fixed needle afterward for a more natural simulation. ## Shape Optimization - If the effect of deleting the fixed needle is not satisfactory, consider using shape optimization. - This method prevents further deformation, maintaining the current simulation form. ## Grid Arrangement - After creating all clothes on the plate, utilize the **reset grid** function to arrange the grid neatly. - A neat grid arrangement results in smoother fabric wrinkles. ## Conclusion - The triangular grid may appear rough but provides more texture. - This concludes the details on creating a scarf in Marvelous Designer. - Feel free to try making one, and see you next time! ```
